title: $f$-GRPO & Beyond: Divergence-Based Reinforcement Learning Algorithms for General LLM Alignment
claim: Different alignment settings share one view: each objective estimates a divergence between aligned and unaligned distributions, and a hybrid objective combines them.
layout: 3 panels: two top side-by-side, one wide bottom; math in boxes
description: Three light-blue dashed panels. Top-left is RLVR and top-right is Preference Alignment. Each starts with an antenna icon labeled Information Signal, an equals sign, and an icon for the reward function or for preference data. Below that is a concrete example. The RLVR panel shows a math question with a green correct answer (+1) and a red wrong answer (0). The preference panel shows a harmful prompt with a green refusal (chosen) and a red compliant reply (rejected). Overlapping green and red bell curves represent the aligned and unaligned distributions, with a divergence formula beneath them. Cyan boxes state that each objective, f-GRPO or FDO, is divergence estimation. The bottom Hybrid Alignment panel adds the two signals and gives the f-HAL formula, λ·FDO + (1-λ)·f-GRPO, labeled off-policy and on-policy. Green versus red color coding runs throughout.
caption: Divergence Estimation Framework. Left: In RLVR, rewards induce reward-aligned/unaligned distributions, and $f$-GRPO estimates an $f$-divergence between them. Right: In preference alignment, direct aligners estimate divergences between chosen/rejected distributions. Bottom: $f$-HAL combines both signals into a hybrid on/off-policy objective.
abstract: Recent work shows that preference alignment objectives can be interpreted as divergence estimators between aligned (preferred) & unaligned (less-preferred) distributions, yielding a principled recipe for designing alignment losses. However, this view has so far been limited to preference-based supervision. We extend it to general LLM alignment, including reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR), where alignment feedback is given only as scalar rewards. We introduce $f$-Group Relative Policy Optimization ($f$-GRPO), a class of on-policy RL objectives, and $f$-Hybrid Alignment Loss ($f$-HAL), which combines on-policy reward optimization with off-policy preference supervision. We show that these objectives estimate $f$-divergences between reward-aligned & reward-unaligned distributions induced by above- & below-average reward responses, and prove expected reward improvement after alignment. Empirically, $f$-GRPO improves over GRPO on math-reasoning RLVR tasks, while hybrid $f$-HAL mitigates reward hacking in on-policy safety alignment when verifiable rewards are unavailable and learned reward models must be used.
